_comment: Ground truth for the class-A reference recognizer (src/thalamus/arch/references.py),
written independently of tests/test_arch_references.py per issue #127 part 1 - the
author's own unit coverage is not the oracle that proves it correct.
Each entry names one file under repo/code/refs_fixtures/, the single reference-shaped
token that file carries, and the disposition the recognizer must assign it:
resolved        - a path/symbol the tree holds
dangling        - a path/symbol the tree does not hold, and no sentence excuses it
asserted-absent - a non-resolving name whose own sentence asserts it does not exist
declined        - recognised (dotted-name form) and deliberately judged by nothing
unconsumed      - matched the loose candidate net but no specific form consumed it
`self_test` marks the one entry whose `expected` value is DELIBERATELY WRONG - see

fixtures.note: issue #127 bullet 1 (oracle_parses_whole class): a backticked reference outside every recognised extension must be reported unconsumed, not silently dropped.
issue #127 bullet 2: a class-C referent (a vendor release, shaped as a dotted name) must be recognised and explicitly declined, never judged.
issue #127 bullet 3: a sentence asserting its own referent's absence must never become a finding.
issue #127 bullet 4a: a negation inside a quotation must not suppress a real dangling reference.
issue #127 bullet 4b: a negation belonging to the previous, already-terminated sentence must not suppress a reference that opens the next line.
issue #127 bullet 5: a GitHub-style line-anchor citation is a form the parser does not know, and must be reported rather than silently skipped.

Deliberately WRONG: mod/anchor.py exists in this fixture tree, so the real disposition is resolved. Permanent discrimination control - proves the comparison this case runs can actually tell right from wrong, on every run rather than once.
